newsitem.title: USA: More hires ahead under Rauscher Pierce growth plan.
newsitem.headline: More hires ahead under Rauscher Pierce growth plan.

text.p: The six new hires Rauscher Pierce Refsnes Inc announced Wednesday mark the early stages of a growth plan that could swell the firm's public finance department alone by another 15 bankers over the next five years, the head of that department said.

Dallas-based Rauscher has hired six former Alex. Brown & Sons Inc professionals for its New York office, including former head municipal trader Jerry McNamara. Three other former Alex. Brown professionals have joined McNamara in Rauscher's municipal sales and trading department.

On the public finance side, Rauscher hired Margaret Guarino as a managing director and Bob Foggio as a vice president, Leslie Lynch, an executive vice president and director of public finance at Rauscher, said. Their hiring brings the number of bankers to 37.
"We expect over the next five years to more than double our negotiated commission business," he said.

Of the projected 15 new public finance jobs, Lynch has his eye on three to four candidates he would like to hire by year end. Though unable to speak for the sales and trading side, Lynch said that department will likely grow "commensurately."
Rauscher has always been a public finance-oriented firm, and has been successful in that area when many other firms have not, he said.
"We need to grow our business, and we see opportunities that are being presented by the exodus of other firms in the business to attract very, very good talent that's out there," Lynch said.
Talks with Alex. Brown began about three weeks ago, he said.
"I have already hired four very senior bankers this year," Lynch said. "Margaret and Bob, and then two other people we hired earlier this year from Dillon Read."

The other two bankers were John Crew, a former Dillon Read & Co. managing director, and Catherine Miller, a former vice president at the firm. Both were based out of Dillon Read's Dallas public finance office, he said.
Rauscher currently has public finance offices in California, Arizona, New Mexico, Texas, Florida and Oklahoma, Lynch said.
"And if we were to add the New York/New Jersey corridor we would have a presence in the areas that constitute about 60 percent of the total volume over the past four or five years," he said.
Historically, Rauscher's public finance efforts have focused on the middle market, with the firm undertaking some larger scale clients as well, Lynch said.

"In order for us to break out basically of the mold that we are in right now, to grow, we are going to have to pursue larger clients such as transportation, utilities, (and) housing on a larger scale," he said, adding that the firm is in those areas currently.
In terms of its public finance business, Rauscher could be considered the country's largest regional firm, Lynch said.

"We're a super regional," he said. "We don't want to characterize ourselves as a national firm, but our practice is beginning to look more and more like a national practice that's focused in certain regional markets."

Rauscher now has a strong market share in Texas, New Mexico and Arizona, and is attempting to beef up efforts in Florida and California. Florida has been one of the top four issuers over the past several years, while California has been one of the top one or two, Lynch said.
"So our principal focus in expansion will be in California, Florida and the New York-New Jersey region," he said, adding that the firm will not neglect its current markets.
"We are going to maintain our business that we presently have. We are going to build on top of it with this expansion," Lynch said. "So it's not an either or."

The firm plans to add five or six new bankers in California over the next five years, with the balance of the 15 projected new hires coming on the East Coast and in Texas, the firm's core business area.
